title: The Structured Minimum
prompt:
**Scenario.** A divide-and-conquer solution fails only when n ≥ 16, never below. What is the right minimal-case hunt?

**Which approach is the best fit? The program only needs to print the letter.**

**A)** Keep testing random n = 15 inputs

**B)** Build the structured case: the smallest complete recursion depth (n = 16 = 2^4) with a pattern that forces the failing merge — e.g., all elements arranged to maximize cross-half interaction

**C)** Give up and submit

**D)** Test n = 1000 to confirm scale sensitivity

tests.name: answer
tests.hint: When the bug needs k interacting items, the minimal case is the smallest structured n that triggers the interaction — 2^d for depth-d recursion — with an arrangement aimed at the merge, not random bulk.
